question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $e$ | ${e}^{4}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $4$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{e}^{{e}^{4}}\frac{5\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{5}{4}{\int }_{e}^{{e}^{4}}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{4}{\int }_{1}^{4}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5}{4}\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}\,{|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{5}{8}\cdot {u}^{2}\,{|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{5}{8}({4}^{2}-{1}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{5}{8}\cdot 15 \\  & =\frac{75}{8}\end{aligned}
$$
